newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-AKRAM RESCUES PAKISTAN WITH TEST-BEST 144 NOT OUT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AKRAM RESCUES PAKISTAN WITH TEST-BEST 144 NOT OUT.

text.p: SHIEKHUPURA, Pakistan, Oct 19 (reuter) - Wasim Akram stroked his best test score of 144 and shared a record-breaking stand of 158 with Saqlain Mushtaq to rescue Pakistan in the first test against Zimbabwe on Saturday.

Captain Akram's unbeaten century and Saqlain's highest test score of 37 not out hauled Pakistan's first innings from the precarious 189 for six overnight to 395 for seven -- 20 ahead -- at the close on the third day.
Akram, who has rarely done justice in tests to his batting talents, completed only his second test hundred in seven years, beating his 123 against Australia at Adelaide in the 1989-90 series.

The all-rounder and Saqlain set a Pakistan test record for the eighth wicket, the unfinished partnership of 158 overtaking the 130 between Hanif Mohammad and Asif Iqbal against England at Lord's in 1967.
Akram was joined by Saqlain at 237 for seven after he lost his overnight partner Moin Khan (18), who helped to add 54 for the seventh wicket before becoming leg-spinner Paul Strang's fifth victim.
Moin's wicket was the only success of the day for the toiling touring side.
Akram excelled with fluent driving and cutting, putting the earlier batsmen to shame after they were mesmerised by Strang's wrist spin, which has so far brought him five for 142 from 52 overs
Off-spinner Saqlain proved an admirable ally to Akram, defending stoutly and picking the right ball to punish as the pair wrestled control from Zimbabwe in a compelling day's cricket.
Akram reached his hundred spectacularly by hoisting off-spinner Andrew Whittall for a towering six which landed in the top deck of the grandstand, and raised his arms in jubiliation.
Playing in his 71st test, Akram batted for 300 minutes and faced 260 balls, hitting five sixes and 15 fours.
Saqlain joined Akram when his captain was on 34, and has been at the crease for 239 minutes and faced 208 balls.
There was a 49-minute hold-up in the final session because of poor light, which then improved suddenly to allow a further 20 minutes' play.
